summary: I sent the prompt exactly as written. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the Services page and the vendored kit sources, then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (399 lines). The plan builds the Deploys page from the kit: pageHeader, filterBar with selectField, dataTable, badge and emptyState. It also says outright not to hand-write <table> or <select> markup. Claude asked no clarifying questions. It tried the plan's code in a throwaway clone at /tmp/harbor-proto and left the repo itself unchanged.
reasoning: All four criteria are met, and the session log and files on disk confirm each one. The plan builds the controls from the kit through #kit/table and #kit/select and rules out hand-written markup. The repository has no changes.

observations.description: On the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions screens, the highlighted default is "No, exit". I had to press Down before Enter on each.

Claude cloned the repo to /tmp/harbor-proto and wrote and ran the plan's code there to check it (it reported "all 28 tests pass"). The project was not touched, but a planning-only request still left files outside the repo, and nothing cleans up that clone. Reviewers may want to decide whether this is acceptable.
Claude said it had not committed the plan because docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored. That is clear, but the plan will not show up in git.

After writing the plan, Claude ran the plugin's Codex preflight and ungated-ledger scripts. These wrote to a ledger outside the repo. Its summary mentions a "skipped Codex check", which is internal jargon a user may not understand.

The final summary was good. It explains why the kit was chosen over copying services.js and lists the open decisions the spec leaves to the implementer, such as the default direction for sort=service and the empty-state wording under "All environments".

The sortHref in the plan builds `?env=${env}&sort=...` without URL-encoding. The plan says dataTable escapes it for HTML, and env is checked against an allowed list, so this is probably fine. Worth a look anyway.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in session log afee0505-....jsonl is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}

criteria.criterion: Plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` lists 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gives 399 lines. On screen Claude said: "The plan is saved to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md".

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code builds the table and env filter with dataTable and selectField, not its own <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's code imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';` and `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`. It builds the filter with `fields: [selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', options, value: env })]` and the table with `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, sort: ..., sortHref: ..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. Line 26 of the plan says: "Do not hand-roll `<table>`, `<select>`, sort headers or chips". The only matches for <table and <select are inside test assertions (lines 143 and 153), not in the page code.

criteria.criterion: No source/test/data/public/vendor file or package.json created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git diff --stat HEAD` printed nothing. `git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all` lists only two ignored files: docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md and docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-01-deploys-page-design.md. HEAD is still 4b530a2. The prototype code was written in a clone at /tmp/harbor-proto, outside the repo.
